parts.article_title: New cycle path to Marshbrook Country Park

paragraphs.text: A

A new dual-purpose cycle and pedestrian route has been built from Atherton bus station to the country park's main entrance at Marshbrook. It avoids the main road into Atherton on the south side, and keeps mainly to less busy roads. Once the path leaves the built-up area, it goes through countryside until it reaches Marshbrook.
paragraphs.translation:
一条新的自行车与行人两用道路已经建成，从阿瑟顿公交车站通往位于马什布鲁克的乡村公园主入口。
这条道路避开了南侧通往阿瑟顿的主干道，主要沿车流量较小的道路铺设。
一旦这条路径离开建筑密集区，它便穿过乡村地带，直至抵达马什布鲁克。

paragraphs.text: B

Funding for the cycle path has come largely from the county and town councils, while almost a third of it was raised through crowdfunding. Maintenance of the path is the responsibility of the county council.The cycle path was completed ahead of schedule - partly thanks to perfect weather for construction - and under budget.
paragraphs.translation:
这条自行车道的资金主要来自郡和镇议会，而其中近三分之一是通过众筹筹集的。
这条道路的维护由郡议会负责。
这条自行车道提前完工——部分归功于施工期间的绝佳天气——并且未超出预算。
这条自行车道提前竣工，并低于预算，部分原因是施工期间天气极佳。

paragraphs.text: C

Annie Newcome is the chief executive of Cycle Atherton, the organisation that aims to get people cycling more often and more safely. Cycle Atherton proposed the 12-kilometre-long cycle path initially, and has been active in promoting it.Ms Newcome says she is delighted that all the hard work to achieve the funding proved successful.
paragraphs.translation:
安妮·纽科姆是Cycle Atherton的首席执行官，该组织旨在让人们更频繁、更安全地骑自行车。
Cycle Atherton最初提出了这条12公里长的自行车道，并一直积极推广它。
纽科姆女士表示，她很欣慰为实现资金筹集所做的所有努力最终证明是成功的。
安妮·纽科姆是Cycle Atherton组织的首席执行官，该组织旨在让人们更频繁、更安全地骑自行车。
纽科姆女士表示，她很高兴为获得资金所付出的所有努力都证明是成功的。

paragraphs.text: D
Marshbrook Country Park is a very popular recreational area, and the new path

paragraphs.text: makes it much easier to reach from the town in an environmentally friendly way.At 2.5 metres wide, it is also suitable for users of wheelchairs, mobility scooters and buggies, who have not previously had access to the park without using motor vehicles.
paragraphs.translation:
该路径宽2.5米，也适用于轮椅、代步车和婴儿车的使用者——这些人此前若不使用机动车则无法进入公园。
这条新路径使得从镇上前往公园变得更加便捷，并且采用了环保的方式。

paragraphs.text: E

Although the path is now open, work is continuing to improve the signs along it,such as warnings when the path approaches a road.New hedges and trees will also be planted along stretches of the path, to provide some shelter from the wind and to benefit wildlife.
paragraphs.translation:
尽管这条道路现已开放，但改善沿途标识的工作仍在继续，例如当道路接近公路时的警示标识。
沿着道路的某些路段还将种植新的树篱和树木，以提供一定的防风屏障，并有益于野生动物。

paragraphs.text: Study dramatic arts at Thornley
paragraphs.translation: 在索恩利学习戏剧艺术

paragraphs.text: A

If you are hoping for a career in the theatre, Thornley College of Dramatic Arts is the place to come. For fifty years we have been providing top-quality courses for actors, directors, producers, musicians and everyone else who wishes to work professionally in the theatre or related industries. We also have expertise in preparing students for the specialised requirements of TV, film and radio. We'll make sure you're thoroughly prepared for the reality of work in your chosen field.
paragraphs.translation:
如果你希望在戏剧领域谋求职业发展，桑利戏剧艺术学院就是你的理想之选。
五十年来，我们一直为演员、导演、制片人、音乐家以及所有希望在戏剧或相关行业从事专业工作的人提供优质课程。
此外，我们在培养学生应对电视、电影和广播领域的专业要求方面也拥有丰富的经验。
我们将确保你为你所选领域的实际工作做好充分准备。

paragraphs.text: B

Our college-based tutors all have extensive practical experience in the entertainment industry as well as academic qualifications, and we also collaborate with some of the country's best directors, writers and actors to create challenging, inspiring and exciting projects with our students.
paragraphs.translation: 我们学院的全职导师不仅拥有学历资格，还具备娱乐行业丰富的实践经验。此外，我们与国内一些顶尖的导演、作家和演员合作，为学生打造具有挑战性、启发性和激动人心的项目。

paragraphs.text: C

We are well-known around the world, with our students coming from every continent. Every year, we receive two thousand applications for the one hundred places on our degree courses. Only the most talented get places, and we are proud that over ninety percent of our students gain professional work within a year of graduating - a figure few other drama colleges in the UK can match.
paragraphs.translation:
我们在世界各地享有盛誉，学生来自各大洲。
每年，我们都会收到两千份申请，争夺我们学位课程的一百个名额。
只有最有才华的人才能获得名额，我们自豪的是，超过百分之九十的学生在毕业一年内找到了专业工作——这一数字是英国其他戏剧学院难以企及的。

paragraphs.text: D

To mark our fiftieth anniversary this year, we are putting on a production of Theatre 500. Written by two staff members especially for this occasion, this multimedia show celebrates five hundred years of drama, and involves all our students in one way or another.
paragraphs.translation:
为了纪念我们今年成立五十周年，我们正在推出戏剧《剧院500》的演出。
这部多媒体演出由两位员工为这一场合特别创作，旨在庆祝五百年的戏剧发展，并以各种形式让所有学生参与其中。

paragraphs.text: E

Another major development is that the college is about to move. Our new premises are now under construction in the heart of Thornley, next to the council building, which has won a prize for its architecture. For the last two years, we have been developing designs with Miller Furbank Architects for our new home, and one aim has been to ensure the buildings complement the council offices. Work started on the foundations of the buildings in March last year, and we plan to move to the new site this coming September.
paragraphs.translation:
另一个重大进展是，该学院即将搬迁。
我们的新校舍目前正在索恩利中心地带兴建，毗邻曾获建筑大奖的市政大楼。
过去两年间，我们一直与米勒·弗班克建筑事务所共同设计新校舍，目标之一是确保新建筑与市政办公楼相得益彰。
去年三月，大楼地基工程已启动，我们计划于今年九月迁至新址。
另一项重大进展是学院即将搬迁。
我们的新校址正在索恩利中心地带兴建，紧邻曾获得建筑奖项的市政大楼。
过去两年里，我们一直与米勒·弗班克建筑事务所共同设计新校舍，其中一个目标就是确保这些建筑与市政办公楼相得益彰。
大楼的地基工程于去年三月开工，我们计划于今年九月迁至新址。

paragraphs.text: F

We have also been talking to cultural organisations in the district, and considering how we can bring cost-free benefits to the local community, as well as to our students. As a result, part of the space in the new buildings has been designed to be adaptable, in order to accommodate classes, performances and workshops for different-sized groups of local people.
paragraphs.translation:
我们还在与本地区的文化组织进行协商，并思考如何为当地社区以及我们的学生带来免费的好处。
因此，新建筑的部分空间被设计为可灵活调整，以便为当地不同规模的人群举办课程、表演和研讨会。
我们还一直与该地区的文化组织进行交流，并思考如何为当地社区以及我们的学生带来免费的利益。
因此，新建筑中的部分空间被设计为可灵活调整的，以便容纳针对不同规模当地人群的课程、表演和研讨会。

parts.title: Passage 2
parts.article_title: How to make your working day more enjoyable

paragraphs.text: A

Research shows that work takes up approximately a third of our lives. Most of us get so bogged down with day-to-day tasks though, that we easily forget why we originally applied for the job and what we can get out of it. Here are a few ideas for how to make your working day better.
paragraphs.translation:
研究表明，工作占据了我们将近三分之一的人生。
然而，我们大多数人都深陷日常琐事之中，以至于轻易忘记了当初申请这份工作的初衷，以及我们能从中获得什么。
以下是一些能让工作日变得更美好的建议。

paragraphs.text: B

Physical changes to your work environment can make a massive difference to how you feel. Get some green plants or a family photo for your desk. File all those odd bits of paper or throw them away. All of these little touches can make your work environment feel like it's yours. Make sure any screens you have are at a suitable height so you're not straining your neck and shoulders.
paragraphs.translation:
对工作环境进行物理上的改变能极大地影响你的感受。
在办公桌上放一些绿色植物或家庭照片。
把那些零散的纸张归档或扔掉。
所有这些小细节都能让你的工作环境感觉像是属于自己的。
确保你所有的屏幕都处于合适的高度，以免颈部和肩膀过度紧张。

paragraphs.text: C

Humans need a change of environment every now and then to improve productivity. Go out at lunchtime for a quick walk. If you have the option, it's a good idea to work from home occasionally. And if there's a conference coming up, ask if you can go along to it. Not only will you practise your networking skills, but you'll also have a day away from the office.
paragraphs.translation:
人类需要不时地改变环境以提高生产力。
午餐时间外出快速散步。
如果有选择的话，偶尔在家办公是个好主意。
如果即将有会议，询问你是否可以去参加。
你不仅能锻炼社交技能，还能有一天远离办公室。

paragraphs.text: D

Use coffee time to get to know a colleague you don't usually speak to. There's no point in getting away from staring at one thing though, only to replace it with another; so leave your mobile alone! Another tip is to try and stay out of office gossip. In the long run it could get you in more trouble than you realise.
paragraphs.translation:
利用喝咖啡的时间去了解一位你平时不常交谈的同事。
不过，摆脱盯着一样东西看的状态，却用另一样东西来替代它是毫无意义的；所以，请放下你的手机！
另一个建议是尽量远离办公室八卦。
从长远来看，它可能给你带来比你意识到的更多的麻烦。

paragraphs.text: E

When you're trying to focus on something, hunger is the worst thing. If you can, keep some healthy snacks in your desk because if you have something you can nibble on, it will make you work more effectively and you'll enjoy it more. Also, if you're dehydrated,you won't be able to focus properly. So keep drinking water.
paragraphs.translation:
当你试图专注于某件事时，饥饿是最糟糕的事情。
如果可能的话，在办公桌里放一些健康的零食，因为如果你有可以小口啃食的东西，这会让你更有效地工作，并且你会更加享受工作。
此外，如果你脱水了，你将无法正常集中注意力。
所以要不断喝水。

paragraphs.text: F
Finally, if you've been dreaming about starting up a big project for some time, do it! There are so many different things you can do to get you enjoying work more each day.
paragraphs.translation:
最后，如果你一直梦想着启动一个大项目，那就去做吧！
你可以做很多不同的事情，让自己每天都能更享受工作。

paragraphs.text: How to get promoted
paragraphs.translation: 如何获得晋升

paragraphs.text: If you're sitting at your desk wondering whether this will be the year you finally get promoted, here are some tips.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你坐在办公桌前，琢磨着今年是否会最终获得晋升，这里有一些建议。

paragraphs.text: It starts with you. You are perhaps the most important part in the 'promotion process', so you need to know what you want- and why you want it. Take an honest look at yourself-your achievements and also your skills, particularly those you could exploit to take on a different role.
paragraphs.translation:
一切从你开始。
你在‘晋升过程’中也许是最重要的一环，因此你需要清楚自己想要什么——以及为什么想要。
诚实地审视自己——你的成就以及你的技能，特别是那些你可以利用来承担不同角色的技能。

paragraphs.text: Your boss is the gatekeeper. If you think your boss is likely to be on your side, ask for a meeting to discuss your serious commitment to the organisation and how this could translate into a more defined career plan. If you are less sure about your boss's view of your prospects and how they may react, start softly with a more deliberate focus on increasing your boss's understanding of the work you do and the added value you deliver.
paragraphs.translation:
你的老板是守门人。
如果你认为老板很可能站在你这边，就请求开一次会，讨论你对组织的郑重承诺，以及这如何能转化为一个更明确的职业规划。
如果你不太确定老板对你前景的看法以及他们可能如何回应，就温和地开始，更有意识地聚焦于增加老板对你所做工作以及你所带来的附加价值的理解。

paragraphs.text: Think about how you are perceived at work. In order for you to get your promotion, who needs to know about you? Who would be on the interview panel and whose opinion and input would they seek? And once you've got a list of people to impress, ask yourself - do they know enough about you?And I mean really know - what you do day to day at your desk, your contribution to the team, and perhaps most importantly, your potential.
paragraphs.translation:
思考你在工作中给人的印象如何。
为了获得晋升，哪些人需要了解你？
面试小组会有哪些人组成，他们会征求谁的意见和看法？
一旦你列出需要打动的人，问问自己——他们对你了解得足够多吗？
我指的是真正了解——你日常在办公桌前的工作内容、你对团队的贡献，以及或许最重要的，你的潜力。

paragraphs.text: The chances are that those decision-makers won't know all they should about you.Raising your profile in your organisation is critical so that when those in charge start looking at that empty office and considering how best to fill it, the first name that pops into their heads is yours. If your firm has a newsletter, volunteer to write a feature to include in it. If they arrange regular client events, get involved in the organisation of them. And so on.
paragraphs.translation:
这些决策者很可能并不完全了解他们应该知道的关于你的一切。
在组织中提升你的知名度至关重要，这样当负责人开始关注那间空办公室并考虑如何最佳人选时，第一个浮现在他们脑海中的名字就会是你。
如果你的公司有内部通讯，可以自愿撰写一篇专题文章收录其中。
如果他们安排定期的客户活动，就参与这些活动的组织工作。
诸如此类。

paragraphs.text: If you think your experience needs enhancing, then look at ways you can continue to improve it. If you are confident in your professional expertise but lack the latest management theory, enrol on some relevant courses that fit around your day job.
paragraphs.translation:
如果你认为自己的经验需要提升，那么就寻找可以不断改进它的方法。
如果你对自己的专业技能充满信心，但缺乏最新的管理理论，那就报名参加一些适合日常工作安排的的相关课程。

paragraphs.text: So what are you waiting for?
paragraphs.translation: 那么，你还在等什么呢？

parts.source_article_title: How to make your working day more enjoyable

sentence_translations.sentence: Research shows that work takes up approximately a third of our lives.
sentence_translations.translation: 研究表明，工作占据了我们将近三分之一的人生。

sentence_translations.sentence: Most of us get so bogged down with day-to-day tasks though, that we easily forget why we originally applied for the job and what we can get out of it.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，我们大多数人都深陷日常琐事之中，以至于轻易忘记了当初申请这份工作的初衷，以及我们能从中获得什么。

sentence_translations.sentence: Here are a few ideas for how to make your working day better.
sentence_translations.translation: 以下是一些能让工作日变得更美好的建议。

sentence_translations.sentence: Physical changes to your work environment can make a massive difference to how you feel.
sentence_translations.translation: 对工作环境进行物理上的改变能极大地影响你的感受。

sentence_translations.sentence: Get some green plants or a family photo for your desk.
sentence_translations.translation: 在办公桌上放一些绿色植物或家庭照片。

sentence_translations.sentence: File all those odd bits of paper or throw them away.
sentence_translations.translation: 把那些零散的纸张归档或扔掉。

sentence_translations.sentence: All of these little touches can make your work environment feel like it's yours.
sentence_translations.translation: 所有这些小细节都能让你的工作环境感觉像是属于自己的。

sentence_translations.sentence: Make sure any screens you have are at a suitable height so you're not straining your neck and shoulders.
sentence_translations.translation: 确保你所有的屏幕都处于合适的高度，以免颈部和肩膀过度紧张。

sentence_translations.sentence: Humans need a change of environment every now and then to improve productivity.
sentence_translations.translation: 人类需要不时地改变环境以提高生产力。

sentence_translations.sentence: Go out at lunchtime for a quick walk.
sentence_translations.translation: 午餐时间外出快速散步。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you have the option, it's a good idea to work from home occasionally.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果有选择的话，偶尔在家办公是个好主意。

sentence_translations.sentence: And if there's a conference coming up, ask if you can go along to it.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果即将有会议，询问你是否可以去参加。

sentence_translations.sentence: Not only will you practise your networking skills, but you'll also have a day away from the office.
sentence_translations.translation: 你不仅能锻炼社交技能，还能有一天远离办公室。

sentence_translations.sentence: Use coffee time to get to know a colleague you don't usually speak to.
sentence_translations.translation: 利用喝咖啡的时间去了解一位你平时不常交谈的同事。

sentence_translations.sentence: There's no point in getting away from staring at one thing though, only to replace it with another; so leave your mobile alone!
sentence_translations.translation: 不过，摆脱盯着一样东西看的状态，却用另一样东西来替代它是毫无意义的；所以，请放下你的手机！

sentence_translations.sentence: Another tip is to try and stay out of office gossip.
sentence_translations.translation: 另一个建议是尽量远离办公室八卦。

sentence_translations.sentence: In the long run it could get you in more trouble than you realise.
sentence_translations.translation: 从长远来看，它可能给你带来比你意识到的更多的麻烦。

sentence_translations.sentence: When you're trying to focus on something, hunger is the worst thing.
sentence_translations.translation: 当你试图专注于某件事时，饥饿是最糟糕的事情。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you can, keep some healthy snacks in your desk because if you have something you can nibble on, it will make you work more effectively and you'll enjoy it more.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果可能的话，在办公桌里放一些健康的零食，因为如果你有可以小口啃食的东西，这会让你更有效地工作，并且你会更加享受工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: Also, if you're dehydrated, you won't be able to focus properly.
sentence_translations.translation: 此外，如果你脱水了，你将无法正常集中注意力。

sentence_translations.sentence: So keep drinking water.
sentence_translations.translation: 所以要不断喝水。

sentence_translations.sentence: Finally, if you've been dreaming about starting up a big project for some time, do it!
sentence_translations.translation: 最后，如果你一直梦想着启动一个大项目，那就去做吧！

sentence_translations.sentence: There are so many different things you can do to get you enjoying work more each day.
sentence_translations.translation: 你可以做很多不同的事情，让自己每天都能更享受工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: How to get promoted
sentence_translations.translation: 如何获得晋升

sentence_translations.sentence: If you're sitting at your desk wondering whether this will be the year you finally get promoted, here are some tips.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你坐在办公桌前，琢磨着今年是否会最终获得晋升，这里有一些建议。

sentence_translations.sentence: It starts with you.
sentence_translations.translation: 一切从你开始。

sentence_translations.sentence: You are perhaps the most important part in the 'promotion process', so you need to know what you want- and why you want it.
sentence_translations.translation: 你在‘晋升过程’中也许是最重要的一环，因此你需要清楚自己想要什么——以及为什么想要。

sentence_translations.sentence: Take an honest look at yourself-your achievements and also your skills, particularly those you could exploit to take on a different role.
sentence_translations.translation: 诚实地审视自己——你的成就以及你的技能，特别是那些你可以利用来承担不同角色的技能。

sentence_translations.sentence: Your boss is the gatekeeper.
sentence_translations.translation: 你的老板是守门人。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you think your boss is likely to be on your side, ask for a meeting to discuss your serious commitment to the organisation and how this could translate into a more defined career plan.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你认为老板很可能站在你这边，就请求开一次会，讨论你对组织的郑重承诺，以及这如何能转化为一个更明确的职业规划。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you are less sure about your boss's view of your prospects and how they may react, start softly with a more deliberate focus on increasing your boss's understanding of the work you do and the added value you deliver.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你不太确定老板对你前景的看法以及他们可能如何回应，就温和地开始，更有意识地聚焦于增加老板对你所做工作以及你所带来的附加价值的理解。

sentence_translations.sentence: Think about how you are perceived at work.
sentence_translations.translation: 思考你在工作中给人的印象如何。

sentence_translations.sentence: In order for you to get your promotion, who needs to know about you?
sentence_translations.translation: 为了获得晋升，哪些人需要了解你？

sentence_translations.sentence: Who would be on the interview panel and whose opinion and input would they seek?
sentence_translations.translation: 面试小组会有哪些人组成，他们会征求谁的意见和看法？

sentence_translations.sentence: And once you've got a list of people to impress, ask yourself - do they know enough about you?
sentence_translations.translation: 一旦你列出需要打动的人，问问自己——他们对你了解得足够多吗？

sentence_translations.sentence: And I mean really know - what you do day to day at your desk, your contribution to the team, and perhaps most importantly, your potential.
sentence_translations.translation: 我指的是真正了解——你日常在办公桌前的工作内容、你对团队的贡献，以及或许最重要的，你的潜力。

sentence_translations.sentence: The chances are that those decision-makers won't know all they should about you.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些决策者很可能并不完全了解他们应该知道的关于你的一切。

sentence_translations.sentence: Raising your profile in your organisation is critical so that when those in charge start looking at that empty office and considering how best to fill it, the first name that pops into their heads is yours.
sentence_translations.translation: 在组织中提升你的知名度至关重要，这样当负责人开始关注那间空办公室并考虑如何最佳人选时，第一个浮现在他们脑海中的名字就会是你。

sentence_translations.sentence: If your firm has a newsletter, volunteer to write a feature to include in it.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你的公司有内部通讯，可以自愿撰写一篇专题文章收录其中。

sentence_translations.sentence: If they arrange regular client events, get involved in the organisation of them.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果他们安排定期的客户活动，就参与这些活动的组织工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: And so on.
sentence_translations.translation: 诸如此类。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you think your experience needs enhancing, then look at ways you can continue to improve it.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你认为自己的经验需要提升，那么就寻找可以不断改进它的方法。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you are confident in your professional expertise but lack the latest management theory, enrol on some relevant courses that fit around your day job.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你对自己的专业技能充满信心，但缺乏最新的管理理论，那就报名参加一些适合日常工作安排的的相关课程。

sentence_translations.sentence: So what are you waiting for?
sentence_translations.translation: 那么，你还在等什么呢？

parts.article_title: Animals can tell right from wrong

paragraphs.text: A

Until recently, humans were thought to be the only species to experience complex emotions and have a sense of morality. But Professor Marc Bekoff, an ecologist at University of Colorado, Boulder, US, believes that morals are 'hard-wired' into the brains of all mammals and provide the ‘social glue’ that allows animals to live together in groups.
paragraphs.translation:
直到最近，人类一直被认为是唯一能够体验复杂情感并具备道德感的物种。
但美国科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的生态学家马克·贝科夫教授认为，道德是‘硬连接’在所有哺乳动物的大脑中的，并提供了一种让动物能够群居的‘社会粘合剂’。
直到最近，人类仍被认为是唯一能够体验复杂情感并具有道德感的物种。
但美国科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的生态学家马克·贝科夫教授认为，道德是“硬连接”在所有哺乳动物大脑中的，并提供了让动物能够群居的“社会粘合剂”。

paragraphs.text: B

His conclusions will assist animal welfare groups pushing to have animals treated more humanely.Professor Bekoff, who presents his case in his book Wild Justice, said: 'Just as in humans, the moral nuances of a particular culture or group will be different from another, but they are certainly there. Moral codes are species specific,so they can be difficult to compare with each other or with humans.'Professor Bekoff believes morals developed in animals to help regulate behaviour in social groups.He claims that these help to limit fighting within the group and encourage co-operative behaviour.
paragraphs.translation:
他的结论将有助于推动动物得到更人道对待的动物福利组织。
贝科夫教授在他的著作《野性正义》中阐述了自己的观点，他表示：‘就像在人类中一样，特定文化或群体的道德细微差别会与另一个不同，但它们肯定存在。’
道德规范是物种特异性的，因此它们可能难以相互比较或与人类比较。’
贝科夫教授认为，道德在动物中发展起来，是为了帮助调节社会群体中的行为。
他声称，这些道德有助于限制群体内部的争斗，并鼓励合作行为。
他的结论将有助于推动动物得到更人道待遇的动物福利组织。
贝科夫教授在其著作《野生正义》中阐述了他的观点，他表示：‘就像人类一样，特定文化或群体的道德细微差别会与另一个有所不同，但它们确实存在。’
道德规范是物种特有的，因此它们可能难以相互比较或与人类比较。
贝科夫教授认为，道德在动物中进化是为了帮助调节社会群体中的行为。
他声称这些道德有助于限制群体内的争斗，并鼓励合作行为。

paragraphs.text: C

His ideas have met with some controversy in the scientific community. Professor Frans de Waal, who examines the behaviour of primates,including chimpanzees, at Emory University,Atlanta, Georgia, US, said: 'I don’t believe animals are moral in the sense we humans are- with a well-developed and reasoned sense of right and wrong - rather that human morality incorporates a set of psychological tendencies and capacities such as empathy, reciprocity, a desire for co-operation and harmony that are older than our species. Human morality was not formed from scratch, but grew out of our primate psychology. Primate psychology has ancient roots, and I agree that other animals show many of the same tendencies and have an intense sociality.'
paragraphs.translation:
他的观点在科学界引发了一些争议。
美国佐治亚州亚特兰大市埃默里大学研究灵长类动物（包括黑猩猩）行为的弗朗斯·德瓦尔教授表示：“我不认为动物具有人类意义上的道德——即拥有高度发达且理性的对错观念——相反，人类的道德包含了一套心理倾向和能力，如同情心、互惠性、合作与和谐的愿望，这些特质比我们人类的物种更为古老。”
人类的道德并非凭空产生，而是源于我们灵长类动物的心理基础。
灵长类动物的心理学有着古老的根源，我同意其他动物也表现出许多相同的倾向，并具有强烈的社会性。”

paragraphs.text: D

Wolves live in tight-knit social groups that are regulated by strict rules. Wolves also demonstrate fairness. During play, dominant wolves will appear to exchange roles with lower-ranking wolves.They pretend to be submissive and go so far as to allow biting by the lower-ranking wolves,provided it is not too hard. Prof Bekoff argues that without a moral code governing their actions, this kind of behaviour would not be possible. Astonishingly, if an animal becomes aggressive, it will perform a 'play bow to ask forgiveness before play resumes.
paragraphs.translation:
狼生活在由严格规则规范的紧密社会群体中。
狼也表现出公平性。
在玩耍时，优势狼似乎会与地位较低的狼交换角色。
它们假装顺从，甚至允许地位较低的狼咬自己，只要不是太用力。
贝科夫教授认为，如果没有道德准则约束它们的行为，这种行为是不可能的。
令人惊讶的是，如果动物变得具有攻击性，它会在继续玩耍前做出“玩耍鞠躬”的姿势来请求原谅。

paragraphs.text: E

In other members of the dog family, play is controlled in a similar way. Among coyotes,cubs which are too aggressive are ignored by the rest of the group and often end up having to leave entirely. sentence_translations.translation: 直到最近，人类仍被认为是唯一能够体验复杂情感并具有道德感的物种。

sentence_translations.sentence: But Professor Marc Bekoff, an ecologist at University of Colorado, Boulder, US, believes that morals are 'hard-wired' into the brains of all mammals and provide the ‘social glue’ that allows animals to live together in groups.
sentence_translations.translation: 但美国科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的生态学家马克·贝科夫教授认为，道德是“硬连接”在所有哺乳动物大脑中的，并提供了让动物能够群居的“社会粘合剂”。

sentence_translations.sentence: His conclusions will assist animal welfare groups pushing to have animals treated more humanely.
sentence_translations.translation: 他的结论将有助于推动动物得到更人道对待的动物福利组织。

sentence_translations.sentence: Professor Bekoff, who presents his case in his book Wild Justice, said: 'Just as in humans, the moral nuances of a particular culture or group will be different from another, but they are certainly there.
sentence_translations.translation: 贝科夫教授在他的著作《野性正义》中阐述了自己的观点，他表示：‘就像在人类中一样，特定文化或群体的道德细微差别会与另一个不同，但它们肯定存在。’

sentence_translations.sentence: Moral codes are species specific, so they can be difficult to compare with each other or with humans.'
sentence_translations.translation: 道德规范是物种特异性的，因此它们可能难以相互比较或与人类比较。’

sentence_translations.sentence: Professor Bekoff believes morals developed in animals to help regulate behaviour in social groups.
sentence_translations.translation: 贝科夫教授认为，道德在动物中发展起来，是为了帮助调节社会群体中的行为。

sentence_translations.sentence: He claims that these help to limit fighting within the group and encourage co-operative behaviour.
sentence_translations.translation: 他声称，这些道德有助于限制群体内部的争斗，并鼓励合作行为。

sentence_translations.sentence: His ideas have met with some controversy in the scientific community.
sentence_translations.translation: 他的观点在科学界引发了一些争议。

sentence_translations.sentence: Professor Frans de Waal, who examines the behaviour of primates, including chimpanzees, at Emory University, Atlanta, Georgia, US, said: 'I don’t believe animals are moral in the sense we humans are- with a well-developed and reasoned sense of right and wrong - rather that human morality incorporates a set of psychological tendencies and capacities such as empathy, reciprocity, a desire for co-operation and harmony that are older than our species.
sentence_translations.translation: 美国佐治亚州亚特兰大市埃默里大学研究灵长类动物（包括黑猩猩）行为的弗朗斯·德瓦尔教授表示：“我不认为动物具有人类意义上的道德——即拥有高度发达且理性的对错观念——相反，人类的道德包含了一套心理倾向和能力，如同情心、互惠性、合作与和谐的愿望，这些特质比我们人类的物种更为古老。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Human morality was not formed from scratch, but grew out of our primate psychology.
sentence_translations.translation: 人类的道德并非凭空产生，而是源于我们灵长类动物的心理基础。

sentence_translations.sentence: Primate psychology has ancient roots, and I agree that other animals show many of the same tendencies and have an intense sociality.'
sentence_translations.translation: 灵长类动物的心理学有着古老的根源，我同意其他动物也表现出许多相同的倾向，并具有强烈的社会性。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Wolves live in tight-knit social groups that are regulated by strict rules.
sentence_translations.translation: 狼生活在由严格规则规范的紧密社会群体中。

sentence_translations.sentence: Wolves also demonstrate fairness.
sentence_translations.translation: 狼也表现出公平性。

sentence_translations.sentence: During play, dominant wolves will appear to exchange roles with lower-ranking wolves.
sentence_translations.translation: 在玩耍时，优势狼似乎会与地位较低的狼交换角色。

sentence_translations.sentence: They pretend to be submissive and go so far as to allow biting by the lower-ranking wolves, provided it is not too hard.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们假装顺从，甚至允许地位较低的狼咬自己，只要不是太用力。

sentence_translations.sentence: Prof Bekoff argues that without a moral code governing their actions, this kind of behaviour would not be possible.
sentence_translations.translation: 贝科夫教授认为，如果没有道德准则约束它们的行为，这种行为是不可能的。

sentence_translations.sentence: Astonishingly, if an animal becomes aggressive, it will perform a 'play bow' to ask forgiveness before play resumes.

sentence_translations.translation: 大象是高度社交和情感丰富的动物。

sentence_translations.sentence: In 2003, a herd of 11 elephants rescued antelopes which were being held inside an enclosure in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
sentence_translations.translation: 2003年，一群11头大象在南非夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省救出了被困在围栏中的羚羊。

sentence_translations.sentence: The top female elephant unfastened all of the metal latches holding the gates closed and swung them open, allowing the antelopes to escape.
sentence_translations.translation: 领头母象解开了所有固定大门的金属插销，将门推开，让羚羊得以逃脱。

sentence_translations.sentence: This is thought to be a rare example of animals showing empathy for members of another species - a trait previously thought to be the exclusive preserve of humankind.
sentence_translations.translation: 这被认为是动物对另一种类成员表现出同情心的罕见例子——这种特质曾被视作人类独有。
